free_tier.notes: the size of the monthly allowance is not stated on the pages read: unverified

record.tooling: Puter.js, puter.ai.chat(prompt, {model}) from a browser or Node.js; there are no API keys, and each user's own Puter account carries the cost. A REST route for a non-browser client was not read
record.chaining: pairs with browser apps; the cost lands on the signed-in or guest account, not on a developer key

limits.value: AI requests per 10 s: 20 anonymous, 30 free, 200 paid; concurrent AI requests: 2 anonymous, 3 free, 20 paid

record.binding_note: the guest-account ceiling of 20 requests per 10 s and 2 concurrent binds; the monthly credit is a second, unquantified gate

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the rate-limit page names an anonymous tier that is a temporary (guest) account, and the tutorial says users authenticate with their Puter account; whether a guest account can spend the monthly allowance on chat, and what a full signup collects, were not read

record.reliability_note: a call that runs out of credit answers 402 insufficient_funds and the SDK shows the user an upgrade prompt
record.confidence_note: all values are from first-party documentation; no request was sent to a Puter endpoint

evidence.quote: Puter.js uses the [User-Pays model](https://docs.puter.com/user-pays-model/), where users authenticate with their Puter account and cover their own AI costs.
evidence.proved: AI calls are made under each user's Puter account with no developer API key

evidence.quote: - Every user starts with a free monthly allowance, enough to test out the platform and use apps built with Puter.js.
evidence.proved: every user has a free monthly allowance, with no number given

evidence.quote: Where a table shows three numbers, they are paid / free / anonymous. Paid is any subscription tier. Anonymous is a temporary (guest) account.
evidence.proved: anonymous means a temporary guest account
AI requests per 10 s are 200 paid, 30 free and 20 anonymous
concurrent AI requests are 20 paid, 3 free and 2 anonymous
a keyless POST on 2026-11-10 answered 200 with an empty body, so the recorded base URL is not a completion route

free_tier.stated: Free tier shown on puter.com as '25 MB Storage' (the 100 GB / 500 GB / 2 TB figures on that page are the paid tiers. Verified by reading the raw HTML, not the rendered summary). Developer-side cost is $0: 'Puter doesn't charge developers for infrastructure. Storage, database, and AI usage are metered to each signed-in user's own Puter account.'.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap: not documented, but the free allowance is 25 MB

egress.terms: Not metered per-GB to the developer; metered to the end user's Puter allowance. No egress line found.

record.tooling: Puter.js. A single <script> tag or the @heyputer/puter.js npm module, keyless. puter.fs.write / read / mkdir give a browser-side filesystem API; auth is 'sign in with Puter'. No S3/WebDAV/SFTP shim.
record.chaining: The interesting multiplier is the opposite of the usual one: because storage is metered to each signed-in user's account, an app with N users gets N x (that user's allowance) and the developer pays nothing. But the free allowance per user is 25 MB, so the chain only works if the app also controls the user accounts. I.e. it is a way to make storage free for an app's users, not a way to get 10 TiB.

limits.value: per-object-cap: not documented, but the free allowance is 25 MB

record.limits_note: per-object-cap: not documented, but the free allowance is 25 MB total, which is the real cap. Request-rate: the vendor states that 'Anti-abuse, rate limiting, and fraud detection are also built into the Puter account layer, so bots and fake sign-ups are filtered before they reach your app'. In neutral terms, its signup layer screens for excess use and automated signups, so free identities are NOT unlimited here. Retention: not documented.
record.reliability_note: Explicitly blocks the several-accounts route: Puter markets that 'usage is metered to each user's own account, so a bad actor has no free resources to farm', plus automated-signup filtering. That removes the second-account allowance this niche usually relies on.

evidence.proved: free tier '25 MB Storage'; paid tiers 100 GB / 500 GB / 2 TB
'Storage, database, and AI usage are metered to each signed-in user's own Puter account, so your costs don't grow with your user count'
puter.fs.write / puter.fs.read / puter.fs.mkdir cloud storage API
